# Economics comparison: what each route costs, earns and demands of your time

*Version 1.2 · 12 October 2026 · 15–20 minutes. The tables below are generated by `models/route_economics.py`. Rerun that script after changing any assumption.*

## How to read this

**Six different quantities, never mixed:**

| Quantity | Meaning | Where it appears |
|---|---|---|
| **Revenue** | What clients pay you, **excluding VAT** | "Revenue / month" |
| **VAT** | Money you collect for the state from Latvian clients. It is not income. EU business clients are invoiced without VAT (reverse charge), and non-EU clients are outside Latvian VAT [S122] | "VAT collected… (pass-through)" |
| **Cash expenses** | Tools, API credits, insurance and bookkeeping (fixed), plus per-engagement costs and marketplace fees (variable) | "Cash costs / month" |
| **Operating profit** | Revenue − cash expenses − bad debt/refunds. **Before** your own taxes and social contributions | "Operating profit / month" |
| **Owner time** | Your hours: delivery including rework, selling (counted per *won* engagement, so failed pitches are included), retainer work and 6 h/month of admin | "Owner hours / month" |
| **Take-home** | What reaches you after Latvian social contributions and income tax, under three set-ups: self-employed general regime; micro-enterprise tax; SIA paying all profit as dividends | "Take-home" rows |

A payment-processing fee is **not** the main deduction. For a service business, the big ones are your unpaid selling time, taxes and contributions.

**Where the inputs come from.**

| Input | Value used | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| R2 price | €3,000 newcomer base; €4,000 with a track record | A 2-day Claude Code course costs €890 per person from an Anthropic partner [S128], so 5 people ≈ €4,450. Marketplace team workshops cost $250 (2 h) to $900 (full day) [S129] |
| R1 price, base | €2,500 per engagement | Deliberately far below specialist LLM audits ($16k–50k, 5–25 days [S130]), because it is a **limited review, not an audit** |
| R3 price, base | €3,500 audit + €1,200/month retainer (high: €5,000 + €1,800) | Above QA tooling (~$35 per agent-seat per month [S134]); no observed market price for independent evaluation, so a pure **assumption** |
| R4 price | €600 newcomer base; €1,000 with reviews; 10% marketplace fee (15% in low and adverse cases) | **Assumption.** The Upwork filing shows category growth, not prices [S127]. Upwork's fee is variable, 0–15%, plus bid credits at $0.15 each [S140] |
| Win rates, hours, months to first sale | **Base = newcomer** without track record or warm contacts; **high = with a network or strong public proof**; low = adverse | **Assumptions**, revised downward after an independent commercial review. They are the least certain inputs and the main thing the validation plans measure |
| Taxes | VAT 21%; self-employed contributions: below €780/month, 10% pension only; from €780, 31.07% on €780 plus 10% on the excess; income tax 25.5% then 33% above €105,300/yr; micro-enterprise tax 25% of turnover; company income tax 20% of distributed profit | [S100][S122][S123][S124][S125] |
| Opportunity cost | Latvian professionals €13.04/h gross, about **€8.69/h net** (Calculation: after 10.5% employee contributions [S100] and 25.5% PIT); EU €24.40/h gross. **Your own net employment or contracting rate is the real benchmark (unknown)** | [S126][S100] |

**Simplifications to keep in mind.**
- Each route is modelled as **one person**, starting from zero clients.
- Retainers build up over time. "Steady state" means after the ramp-up. "First 12 months" includes the months with no sales.
- Owner time is unpaid until clients pay.
- Not tax advice: the self-employed calculation uses the minimum-contribution option and ignores deductible expenses beyond those modelled.

## The answer in one table (base case = newcomer)

| Route | Revenue/month once steady | Owner hours/month | Take-home/month once steady | €/owner-hour once steady | **€/owner-hour, first 12 months: newcomer / with network** | First 12 months, adverse* | Months to first sale |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 Agent risk review (limited) | €1,475 | 43 | €783 | €18.3 | **€7.2 / €36.3** | loss (−€6.4/h) | 6 |
| R2 Coding-agent enablement | €1,500 | 42 | €832 | €20.0 | **€11.2 / €27.6** | loss (−€2.8/h) | 6 |
| R3 Support-agent evaluation | €2,422 | 50 | €1,379 | €27.4 | **€3.2 / €23.4** | loss (−€9.6/h) | 8 |
| R4 Small workflow automations | €750 | 31 | €470 | €15.0 | **€9.9 / €23.2** | loss (−€1.3/h) | 3 |
| R5 Learn first (3 months) | €0 | 40–100 (120–300 in total) | −€360 to −€1,440 total | — | — | — | — |

*The adverse case combines six shocks at once: half the sales, prices 30% lower, double rework, double selling effort, a 3-month-longer ramp and +5 points of marketplace fee. "First 12 months" includes setup and the months with no sales; when cash is negative, the figure shown is pre-tax cash per hour.

**What the numbers say (Interpretation).**
1. **Access to buyers matters more than the route.**
   - For a newcomer, first-year pay is about **€3–11 per hour after tax**: roughly the net pay of an average Latvian professional (≈ €8.7/h), or less.
   - With warm access or strong proof, the same routes pay **€23–36 per hour** in year one.
   - Testing is therefore mainly about finding out *which of these two worlds you are in*, cheaply.
2. **None of the routes is a business in year one for a newcomer.** Steady-state take-home is about €470–1,380 a month for 31–50 hours. That is a side income.
3. **Cash risk is small; time risk is large.**
   - Setup cash is €150–900 and monthly fixed costs are €110–280.
   - What you risk is **about 215–285 hours** of unpaid preparation, selling and admin before the first sale on R1–R3 (6–8 months at 40–60 selling hours per won engagement), and about 80 hours on R4.
4. **The adverse first year is a loss on every route.** You would lose the time and a few hundred to a few thousand euros. The validation plans' stop rules exist to cut that loss early.
5. **Price matters more than rework.** In every base case, a 30% lower price costs more take-home than doubled rework. Rework costs *time*, not cash.
6. **R2 has the best newcomer first year** (€11.2/h). It is credible only for a professional developer.
7. **R3 has the best steady state but the worst first year**, because of the 8-month ramp. It only makes sense with existing support-industry contacts.
8. **Tax set-up barely changes the ranking.**
   - At these low incomes the self-employed regime is the cheapest: below €780 a month, only a 10% pension contribution is due [S125].
   - The micro-enterprise tax gives the same or less take-home (−€161 to +€5 a month in base cases). It is available only without EU VAT-registered clients, and is lost from the next tax year otherwise [S124].
   - An SIA paying everything out as dividends gives more than the self-employed regime only once profit is higher (R1–R3 base and all high cases). It provides no social insurance. Treat that row as an upper bound, not advice.

---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 Agent risk review (limited) | €2,950 | 60 | €1,722 | €28.9 | €10.4 | 4 |
| R2 Coding-agent enablement | €4,000 | 62 | €2,418 | €38.9 | €15.6 | 4 |
| R3 Support-agent evaluation | €3,670 | 66 | €2,177 | €33.1 | €13.3 | 6 |
| R4 Small workflow automations | €3,400 | 69 | €1,894 | €27.4 | €12.6 | 2 |
| R5 Learn first (3 months) | €0 | 40–100 | −€360 to −€1,440 total | — | — | — |

*Adverse case: half the sales, prices 30% lower, double rework and double the selling effort, all at once.

**What the numbers say (Interpretation).**
1. **In the base case, every route is a modest part-time income, not a business.** About €1,700–2,400 a month for 60–70 hours. That beats the Latvian professional average per hour (€13.04 [S126]) and is around or above the EU average (€24.40).
2. **The adverse case is roughly break-even with an ordinary Latvian job.** Under the "low" assumptions, R1, R2 and R4 never reach €13/h. The routes are attractive *only if* sales come at about the base rate, which is exactly what is unknown.
3. **Cash risk is small; time risk is large.**
   - Setup cash is €150–900 and monthly fixed costs are €110–280, so no route can lose much money.
   - What you can lose is **about 180–250 hours** of unpaid preparation, selling and admin before the first sale in the R1–R3 base cases: 4–6 months, at 25–45 selling hours per won engagement. In R4 it is about 50 hours.
4. **Price matters more than rework.** In every base case, a 30% lower price costs more take-home than doubled rework. Rework costs *time*, not cash.
5. **R2 has the highest pay per hour.** Its base case requires a €4,000 engagement, which is credible only for a professional developer.
6. **R3 is the slowest to pay back.** In base-case 12-month operating cash it is the weakest (€10,454 before tax), because of the 6-month ramp. With retainers it is the strongest *once* established.
7. **Tax set-up barely changes the ranking.**
   - The micro-enterprise tax is within €10–125 a month of the self-employed regime in the base cases. It is lost as soon as you serve an EU VAT-registered client [S124].
   - An SIA distributing everything as dividends leaves more cash in the high cases, but provides no social insurance. Treat that row as an upper bound, not advice.
